metadata.proof: SOURCE: Any authenticated user (including customer role) with a valid token. SINK: db.query(ServiceType).all() returns all rows. The endpoint uses get_current_user (any authenticated user) instead of require_roles with a restricted set. A customer can enumerate all service types and read requires_proof and default_duration_minutes — internal operational metadata.

extra.message: Webhook Secrets Returned in API Responses

metadata.proof: SOURCE: WebhookConfig.secret column stored in database. SINK: WebhookConfigOut.secret field included in the Pydantic response model, returned by both POST /api/admin/webhooks and GET /api/admin/webhooks (admin.py:96,107). Although only ops_admin can access these endpoints, the secret field should be write-only (only accepted on create, never returned). Returning the secret in responses increases exposure risk through logging, client-side caching, or compromised admin sessions.

extra.message: Field Worker Privilege Escalation via Insufficient Update Guard

metadata.citation: if req.status is not None or req.assigned_to is not None or req.internal_notes is not None:
metadata.proof: SOURCE: PATCH request body from an authenticated field_worker (IncidentUpdate schema). SINK: The guard at line 174 blocks status, assigned_to, and internal_notes — but the subsequent setattr loop at line 184 iterates over all remaining fields (severity, description, customer_summary, resolution) and writes them unconditionally. The IncidentUpdate schema includes severity, customer_summary, and resolution which are NOT in the blocked set. A field worker can escalate an incident from low to critical severity, set a resolution before the incident is actually resolved, or change customer_summary text.

extra.message: Logout Does Not Invalidate JWT Token

metadata.proof: SOURCE: Authenticated POST /api/auth/logout. SINK: response.delete_cookie('access_token') removes only the HttpOnly cookie. The JWT token itself (a stateless bearer token) is never invalidated server-side — there is no token blacklist, revocation store, or versioned user secret. Additionally, the login endpoint (auth.py:58) returns the raw JWT in the response body: return {'access_token': access_token, ...}. An attacker who has obtained the raw JWT value (via XSS, network sniffing, or the login response) can continue using it in the Authorization header until it naturally expires.
